forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES: Qatar-mediated preparatory meetings held in Doha June 10-15 with Iranian delegates and Qatari mediators coordinating with the US, confirmed by Qatar MFA statements dated June 15 and 18 (Gulf Times, Qatar MFA). On June 15, Qatar MFA welcomed a 'reached agreement' on the MOU framework, which presupposes Iranian presence in a formally mediated session with named representatives — not mere written exchange. Jerusalem Post (June 16) confirms Doha sessions with Iranian delegation before EOD June 16. Resolution criterion (held session or official rescinding of suspension) satisfied.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed convened US-Iran negotiating session occur before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES: June 21-22, 2026 formal US-Iran negotiating session at Bürgenstock, Lake Lucerne, Switzerland. US delegation led by VP Vance, Jared Kushner, Steve Witkoff; Iran delegation led by Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf and FM Araghchi; Pakistan and Qatar as named mediators. Approximately 18-hour session produced joint mediator readout on 'positive and constructive atmosphere', a 60-day roadmap, and a High Level Committee with three technical working groups (nuclear/sanctions/implementation). Independent TIER1 coverage: Al Jazeera (2026-06-22), CNN (2026-06-21), NPR, CBC. Face-to-face with named mediators (Pakistan/Qatar) within the June 10-24 window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar), between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/Al Jazeera/Times of Israel; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Mere relay of written messages, or one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange (strikes both ways) occur in any 48h window before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO: The last direct Israel-Iran two-way exchange occurred June 7-8, 2026 — outside the resolution window (June 10-24). Trump intervened June 8; Israel and Iran issued separate halt declarations the same afternoon. From June 8 onward, the MOU process proceeded (June 12: Pakistan PM announces final text; June 14-15: digital signing; June 17: formal signing by Trump at Versailles and Pezeshkian in Tehran). No TIER1 source reported direct two-way state strikes between June 10 and June 24. War officially ended June 17. Ambiguity rule applied: proxy-only attacks without direct Iran-Israel state strikes do not count.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange — Israeli strikes on Iranian targets AND Iranian strikes on Israeli/Israeli-claimed targets — within any rolling 48h window between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) OR one TIER1 + official Israeli (IDF) or Iranian (IRGC) statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Proxy-only attacks (Hezbollah/Houthi) without direct Iran-Israel state strikes do NOT count; one-directional strikes within the 48h window = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: IDF + IRGC reciprocal strike statements within 48h

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO (early resolution, ambiguity rule applied): Iran declared the US/coalition-designated transit corridor 'unacceptable and dangerous' on June 25; traffic fell from the June 24 peak of 62 transits (Windward AIS) to approximately 5 transits. Mathematical impossibility: with only 6 days remaining to the July 2 horizon and June 25 at ~5 transits, a 50/day 7-day average cannot be achieved. Source conflict >20%: CENTCOM reported 55 transits June 25; Iran and Al Jazeera reported ~5. Per ambiguity rule, source conflict >20% when primary tracker (IMF PortWatch) data unavailable triggers AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Judge ruled early RESOLVE-NO.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

indicators.name: PortWatch/Windward 7-day transit trend rising toward 50/day

forecasts.question: Will mine-countermeasure clearing operations actively commence in Hormuz before EOD 2026-07-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES: CENTCOM press release confirmed mine-countermeasure clearing operations commenced June 16, 2026, one day after MOU digital signing. Multinational: France and UK leading, with Germany, Italy, Japan, Canada, and 15+ nations participating. The Hill reported 'US military starts removing mines from Strait of Hormuz.' Al Jazeera (June 25) published visual guide on minesweeping operations in Hormuz. Resolution criteria clearly satisfied: confirmed commencement, not intent or positioning. Observed well before EOD July 10.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports mine-countermeasure vessels/operations have actively commenced clearing the Strait of Hormuz (US/coalition/third-party) between 2026-06-10 and 2026-07-10.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/CNBC, or a named US/UK/coalition naval/Pentagon statement carried by TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Stated intent, vessel positioning, or planning without confirmed commencement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: First reading 106-0 passed June 1-2; no reports of second or third reading June 10-26. Haredi coalition crisis ongoing: Degel HaTorah/Shas brinkmanship; Netanyahu reportedly wants October election, Shas/UTJ prefer September. No ToI/JPost/Reuters reports of fixed election date or third-reading vote in the 16-day period. Election date band (September 8 - October 20) remains unfixed. Horizon July 15 (19 days); bill still requires second and third readings with a fixed date inserted. Scope updated: resolution now requires both second and third readings completing with a fixed date before EOD July 15 (absorbed from N3, merged at inception). Probability unchanged; no new information shifts the prior.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in second AND final (third) reading, AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after Oct 27 is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: EXCEPTIONAL INTRA-WEEK UPDATE (37-day gap, 2026-05-19 to 2026-06-26). Terminological clarification: voluntary dissolution via the dissolution bill counts as 'dissolves early' — the resolution criterion 'if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27' is satisfied by a coalition-initiated dissolution bill progressing to final vote. Drivers changed fundamentally since May 19: dissolution bill passed first reading 106-0 on June 1-2 (the coalition itself voting to dissolve before the Oct 27 mandatory cycle); Haredi-draft/Basic Law Torah Study brinkmanship ongoing; Maariv polls reportedly show opposition 61/coalition 49 seats. The 106-0 first reading establishes that the coalition expects to dissolve; the remaining uncertainty is whether second and third readings complete with a fixed date before the mandatory October 27 cycle concludes independently. Updated p 0.35 to 0.55. Next Sunday 2026-06-29: full cold-start review.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Voluntary dissolution via Knesset dissolution bill counts as 'dissolves early.' Exceptional intra-week update 2026-06-26 due to 37-day staleness and fundamental change in dissolution bill status.
